title: Psychobiological Predictors of Treatment Satisfaction and Outcomes Following Cardiac Interventions (PVI)
summary:
Even in highly invasive medical procedures such as coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery, treatment outcomes are not solely determined by the clinician’s skills or medical factors. Psychological factors—such as patients’ expectations—also play a significant role. These psychological factors can influence postoperative quality of life. For example, a brief psychological intervention administered prior to cardiac surgery has been shown to optimize patients’ treatment expectations, reduce disease-related impairment, and improve quality of life.

However, it remains unclear to what extent psychobiological predictors—such as patients’ expectations—affect treatment satisfaction and outcomes in the context of cardiac valve interventions or pulmonary vein isolation (PVI). This study aims to address this question. If specific factors (e.g., certain patient expectations) can be identified as relevant predictors of treatment outcomes, the development of a targeted psychological intervention to prepare patients for cardiac procedures could be a promising next step.

Research Questions
1. Do psychobiological predictors assessed at baseline influence or predict treatment outcomes in patients undergoing cardiac interventions?

2. Do psychobiological predictors assessed at baseline influence or predict treatment satisfaction in patients undergoing cardiac interventions?
conditions: Atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter, unspecified

interventions.name:
Patients undergoing a pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) complete psychological questionnaires at three time points (see below). In parallel, biological parameters such as physical activity and basic cardiological diagnostics are assessed.
